strengths: Review634 covered all eleven PDF pages and the complete source, including the all-input converse, separable-space strict gap, operational transfer for every finite E,N, unknown signal family and zero/oscillatory subsequences.

The all-input converse consistently retains the original D0 reference, uses a normalized comparator for Audenaert TRE, discloses its printed proof erratum, and gives an explicit vanishing R_minus envelope without assuming a thermal optimizer for the mixed channel.

Finite physical input/output cuts and exact type subspaces transfer the information bounds to one compound encoder/decoder while enforcing physical expected energy; arbitrary reset orientation, entropy and energy are allowed.

The strict loss gap uses consistent root-fidelity conventions, finite flag chain rules and justified separable-space limits. Signal degradation is used only on the signal, not asserted as an order on mixed channels.

In review634 all twenty packet payloads were verified, and 90 scalar, 72 finite-matrix and 1080 strict-gap controls reproduced byte-identically. Fourteen primary snapshots were pinned, with reading depth recorded.
The prior type-bound attribution and input-tail derivation comments were resolved in this exact PDF. They are not unresolved objections to v2.
weaknesses: The original importance judgment is a strong specialized contribution, not demonstrated field-wide impact. The actual critical-regime minimax curve, optimal strict-gap constant and practical coding implementation remain open.

The search was directed, not exhaustive. No worldwide priority certificate or independent novelty of the combined state-gap inequality was established. Gaussian capacity, Choi norm, Gram/fidelity inequalities, exact-type mechanisms and finite compound coding are prior ingredients.
Selected primary proofs were read; the full imported decoupling/AEP chain, every prerequisite of infinite-dimensional capacity, and all earlier dependency proofs were not independently reconstructed.

The three programs replay supplied finite implementations. They do not construct an operational code, compute capacities, verify an infinite Gaussian Choi form or optimizer, or prove the asymptotic regime. Older scalar controls and auxiliary near/far tests have narrower scopes than the final theorem.

No uniform blocklength or complexity in E,N, no within-code channel variation, no uniformity over all unspecified o(E) paths at fixed energy, and no uniform limit as kappa0 tends to zero, lambda reaches an endpoint, or alpha tends to one or infinity are claimed.

Necessity concerns the complete curve using a growing budget, not every restricted small-budget problem. The zero-temperature subsequences depend on the prior working-paper pure-loss theorem; its earlier assessment is not used as proof.
